issues.translation_quote: Very nice, thank you!
issues.justification: Awkward in English dialogue. Here it means 'That's very kind, thank you' or 'I'm very pleased, thank you,' not 'Very nice.'

issues.source_quote: Товарища Телегина знаете? Передовой человек, верно?
issues.translation_quote: You know Comrade Telegin? A leading man, right?
issues.justification: 'Leading man' evokes an actor/romantic lead in English and weakens the Soviet bureaucratic-praise tone. 'A progressive/leading figure' would better preserve the era-specific register.

issues.translation_quote: Puss in Boots
issues.justification: The Russian is plural ('Cats in Boots'), and the joke depends on multiple cats plus the later budget line 'the cats are in the estimate, but there is no money for boots.' Singular 'Puss in Boots' damages the logic of the gag.

issues.translation_quote: Three cubes and some planks.
issues.justification: This sounds vague and improvised. The line is a dry production-costing comment; 'three cubic meters of boards/lumber for that' would be more natural and precise.

issues.source_quote: Хорошо, это и серьёзно, и в тоже время как-то мобилизует!
issues.translation_quote: Good: it's serious and at the same time somehow mobilizing!
issues.justification: The humor lies in deadpan Soviet officialese. 'Somehow mobilizing' sounds accidentally awkward rather than recognizably bureaucratic; the comic bureaucratic cadence is not successfully carried over.

issues.source_quote: Бабу Ягу со стороны брать не будем, воспитаем в своём коллективе!
issues.translation_quote: We won't bring Baba Yaga in from outside— we'll raise one within our own team!
issues.justification: 'Воспитаем' here means 'we'll cultivate/train one from our own staff,' a joke about producing a witch internally. 'Raise one' suggests rearing a child and distorts the line's workplace humor.

issues.translation_quote: we worked our brain's gray matter
issues.justification: Over-literal phrasing sounds clumsy rather than pompously comic. A more idiomatic English rendering could preserve the mock-scientific bureaucratic humor better.

issues.translation_quote: a certain unknown fellow ... that unknown-unknown
issues.justification: The repeated joke on 'unknown' is preserved only mechanically; 'unknown-unknown' is unnatural in English and doesn't land as dialogue humor.

issues.translation_quote: The broadcast is on!
issues.justification: This misses the comic shock of the whole building hearing the confession over the house PA/radio network. 'You're on the PA' or 'It's going out over the loudspeakers' would convey the situational humor much better.

issues.translation_quote: let's go check the sites
issues.justification: Literal and odd in context. In a House of Culture inspection this would be more naturally 'let's make the rounds' or 'let's inspect the rooms/areas.'

issues.translation_quote: Bears at Rest
issues.justification: A literal title is possible, but it sounds stiff and obscure in English. Since the joke is about a tastelessly 'suitable' painting, a more natural phrasing would help the comedic effect.

issues.translation_quote: the legs isolated!
issues.justification: The line is funny because of its absurd quasi-bureaucratic phrasing. 'Isolate the legs' is too literal and stilted in English without becoming funny; the joke fails to cross effectively.

issues.source_quote: добавьте сюда ещё людей, будет большой, массовый квартет
issues.translation_quote: Add more people here— it'll be a big, mass quartet.
issues.justification: The absurdity is preserved semantically, but 'mass quartet' is not an English comic phrase and lands awkwardly. The joke needs a more performable rendering, e.g. 'make it a large-scale quartet' or similar.

issues.source_quote: А и Б играли на трубе!
issues.translation_quote: A and B were playing the trumpet!
issues.justification: This is an odd stock phrase parody; in English it reads as random nonsense. A more adaptive rendering could better signal that Ogurtsov is speaking in meaningless formulae.

issues.translation_quote: a calm disposition
issues.justification: The Russian is comically bureaucratic/official in a personal context. 'Calm disposition' is too normal and smooth, losing character flavor.

issues.translation_quote: With my healthy collective!
issues.justification: The sense is wrong. He objects to the lyric 'I alone, all alone' because it clashes with being among his 'healthy collective'—i.e. a wholesome team environment. 'With my healthy collective' is opaque and unnatural; the joke and ideological tone are not conveyed.

issues.source_quote: я боялся, что придётся говорить с этой, как её.. Фроловой
issues.translation_quote: I was afraid I'd have to speak with that... what's her name... Frolova
issues.justification: The dismissive 'с этой, как её' is a bit sharper/more insulting than the English. The social slight against Krylova is softened.

issues.source_quote: Во всяком случае, в этом году разговор о личных делах не состоится.
issues.translation_quote: In any case, this year there will be no talk about personal matters.
issues.justification: The line means there will be no discussion/relationship talk this year between them; in English it sounds overly broad and bureaucratic. It weakens the emotional and comic payoff to the grandfather episode.

issues.translation_quote: This is turning into some kind of nonsense.
issues.justification: The idiom carries comic flavor; flattening it to 'nonsense' loses the rustic/buffoonish color of Ogurtsov's speech.

issues.translation_quote: A-oo-sya!
issues.justification: This seems transliterated rather than translated or adapted for performance. As a comic stage cry/noise, it reads oddly on the page and may puzzle viewers.

issues.translation_quote: about five people
issues.justification: 'Пяток' colloquially means 'five or so,' but the scene's comic tone suggests a rough, bossy order. 'About five people' is semantically acceptable yet flattens the brusque colloquialism significantly.

issues.translation_quote: Happy upcoming
issues.justification: 'Happy upcoming' is not idiomatic English holiday speech and repeatedly sounds unnatural. Standard natural renderings like 'Happy New Year in advance' or simply 'Happy New Year' would fit better.

issues.translation_quote: cultural service
issues.justification: Awkward literalism. In this context 'cultural entertainment' or 'public enjoyment' would sound more natural while keeping the official flavor.

issues.source_quote: докладчика не будет... Доклад буду делать лично я
issues.translation_quote: There will be no speaker... I will deliver the address personally
issues.justification: The Soviet-specific distinction between 'докладчик/доклад' and festive entertainment is central to the satire. 'Speaker/address' weakens the bureaucratic pomp and the comic threat of a formal report at a party.

issues.translation_quote: a lecturer from the Society for Dissemination
issues.justification: This is opaque in English and does not communicate the period-specific institution (the Knowledge Society / society for the dissemination of political and scientific knowledge). The joke depends on recognizing a dreary official lecturer.

issues.translation_quote: a little shot
issues.justification: 'A little shot' is awkward and slightly off register. 'A small drink' or 'a little nip' would fit spoken English better.

issues.translation_quote: And look with an armed eye
issues.justification: This famous comic line should sound absurd but intelligible. 'Armed eye' is a calque that risks sounding simply wrong rather than funny in English; 'through an instrument-assisted eye' or another adaptation is needed to make the joke land.

issues.translation_quote: Bye!
issues.justification: In this exchange shouted from the audience, 'Bye!' sounds too literal and odd; something like 'We've done that already!' or a more natural heckle might work better depending on timing.

issues.translation_quote: The Ensemble of Pension and Dance!
issues.justification: The malapropism is crucially funny, but 'Pension and Dance' is not idiomatic enough in English to land cleanly. A more performable adaptation is needed to preserve the joke.

issues.translation_quote: original-genre department
issues.justification: This is a Soviet variety-entertainment term; the translation is incomprehensible in English. The magician's line loses sense and comic setting.

issues.translation_quote: I prepared theses
issues.justification: In English 'theses' sounds academic and odd here. 'Talking points' or 'theses for my report' would be clearer and more idiomatic.

issues.source_quote: работают наши официантки... А они подают большие надежды!
issues.translation_quote: they only serve ice cream? But they serve great promise!
issues.justification: The pun on 'подают' ('serve' / 'show') is mangled. 'Serve great promise' is unidiomatic and the joke does not work in English.

issues.translation_quote: Who doesn't know his historic phrase
issues.justification: Too literal and stiff for comedic emcee patter. The mock-grand style should sound playful in English; this reads like translationese.

issues.translation_quote: Bitter! Bitter!
issues.justification: This wedding cry has no meaning in English if left literally. Since it cues kissing and communal teasing, failure to adapt it is a major humor/cultural-transfer problem.

issues.source_quote: вот сидит паренёк, без пяти минут он- мастер!
issues.translation_quote: Here sits a lad—he's five minutes away from becoming a master!
issues.justification: 'Без пяти минут мастер' is an idiomatic Soviet expression for 'all but a master/almost fully qualified,' echoing the song's five-minute motif. 'Five minutes away' is understandable but too literal and misses the idiomatic flavor.

issues.translation_quote: The New Year is for singing and making merry
issues.justification: Though broadly accurate, the festive lyric register is overly formal/old-fashioned in places throughout the song, and here 'making merry' risks sounding archaic rather than lively and popular.
